ArchiveEntry.description:
Headless-archive shape: one entry in the public archive.

``id`` is the send's Task id (ShortUUID) — the same id /reports uses, so
the two endpoints join naturally. ``public`` mirrors hosted-page
visibility; headless consumers get every curated entry either way and
can filter on it. ``html`` (detail only) is the web-safe render: merge
tags resolved to fallbacks, tracking stripped, unsubscribe links inert.

public.description:
Effective archive visibility, not just the per-email switch.

A publication can be hidden from the archive wholesale, which takes
its sends off the hosted pages and RSS. Reporting the raw
``is_public`` here would tell a headless consumer to publish an
issue the hosted archive refuses to show — one flag, one meaning,
across every surface.

url.description: Hosted post URL, or null when no hosted pages are being served.

PatchedV2Field.description:
Field representation for v2.

The ``internal`` flag is a system-managed marker for built-in fields. v2
only ever exposes user-managed custom fields (the view filters internal
ones out of the queryset), so the flag carries no information for a public
client and is dropped from the serialized shape entirely.

PatchedV2Person.description:
The single Person representation for v2 (list AND detail).

The platform now allows phone-only contacts (SMS), so the base
``PersonListSerializer`` treats ``email`` as optional and enforces an
email-or-phone rule at the object level (a ``non_field_errors`` message).
The v2 public surface is email-addressed only — its create path reads
``validated_data["email"]`` directly and the docs pin email as required —
so re-require it here. Missing email is then a precise field-level
``email`` error rather than the model's ``non_field_errors``.

``id`` is the opaque ``uid`` (the same value used to address the contact in
the URL), NOT the auto-incrementing integer primary key. Exposing the
sequential PK would leak the workspace's contact count and let a client
enumerate contacts, so v2 never surfaces it.

``status`` is the single subscription/deliverability indicator (active,
unsubscribed, bounced, unconfirmed, not_subscribed, cleaned). The
individual read-only flags it is derived from — ``unsubscribed``,
``bounced``, ``marketing_consent`` — are not surfaced separately.
``double_opt_in`` is still accepted on write (it drives the opt-in flow)
but is write-only, so it isn't echoed back.

``tags`` is a flat list of tag names (not tag objects). The write side
(handled in the view, not this serializer) accepts the same list of names.

``extra_data`` holds only user-defined and profile custom fields. The
internal, system-managed fields (created_at, last_activity, source,
open_rate, click_rate, phone_number, status) are surfaced as top-level
keys and never echoed inside ``extra_data`` — see ``V2ExtraPersonDataField``.

PatchedV2Publication.description:
Read shape for a publication.

No subscriber count: under the deviation model a count is a semi-join
against the workspace's whole Person table, and doing one per publication
on every list call would be a full scan per row at production scale. Use
GET /publications/{id}/subscribers (cursor-paginated) to iterate, or an
audience with a publication trigger if you want a maintained count.

PatchedWebhookEndpoint.description:
Shared representation for the signed-webhook endpoints.

Used by both the public v1 API (key auth) and the internal SPA API
(session auth) so the two surfaces can't drift.

PersonIdentifier.description:
Address one contact from the request body rather than the URL.

This is the shape every body-addressed contact endpoint takes — retrieve,
create/update, delete, opt-in, unsubscribe and publications — so the two
ways to name a contact stay identical across all of them.

The two identifiers are the same pair the /people/{id} detail routes
accept: the opaque ``id`` (uid) or the ``email``. Email is what a caller
integrating from their own app usually has on hand, so requiring the uid
would force a lookup round trip just to name someone they can already
identify.

Naming the contact here rather than in the path also keeps email addresses
out of URLs, where they land in access logs, proxy caches and browser
history, and where the characters that are legal in an address but
structural in a URL (``/``, ``?``, ``#``, ``%``) have to be
percent-encoded — which client libraries do for you everywhere except the
path.

Both may be sent; ``id`` wins, since it's the unambiguous one. That is
what lets an update address a contact by id while *changing* its email in
the same request. Neither is a 400 — a body-addressed endpoint with no
address is a mistake, never a request to act on every contact.

PersonPublicationsRequest.description:
Body for POST /api/v2/people/publications.

Omitting ``publications`` makes the call a read. Supplying it applies only
the ids it names, so a partial map can't silently revoke consent for
publications the client didn't mention.

V2AudienceMember.description:
Lightweight member shape for iterating an audience.

Deliberately lean: it exposes only the contact's identity and status —
columns already on the Person row — and avoids the per-contact open/click
rate lookups and the tag / extra_data joins the full contact object does,
which would turn paging through a large audience into an N+1. Fetch a
single contact's full detail from /api/v2/people/{id} when needed.

get.description:
/api/v2/archive — the broadcasts a workspace has published to its
public archive.

The archive only ever contains bulk broadcasts (never automation or
transactional sends), so each row joins to /api/v2/reports by its shared
Task ``id``; this endpoint adds the web-safe render and curation state.

Works in every archive mode (it's authenticated, not a public surface):
curation happens in the archive settings UI; this endpoint serves
whatever was curated. ``url`` is null unless hosted pages are live.

Filtering: ``?public=true`` (the default) returns curated entries only,
``false`` returns the hidden ones, ``all`` returns both.

public archive.

The archive only ever contains bulk broadcasts (never automation or
transactional sends), so each row joins to /api/v2/reports by its shared
Task ``id``; this endpoint adds the web-safe render and curation state.

Works in every archive mode (it's authenticated, not a public surface):
curation happens in the archive settings UI; this endpoint serves
whatever was curated. ``url`` is null unless hosted pages are live.

Filtering: ``?public=true`` (the default) returns curated entries only,

GET /api/v2/audiences — the workspace's audiences and their member counts.

The response always leads with a synthetic "All active subscribers" list
whose ``members`` is the total number of active subscribers in the workspace, then
the saved audiences ordered by member count (largest first). One-time send
audiences (``ad_hoc``) are excluded, matching the app's audience list.

The set is bounded (audiences are plan-limited), so this list is returned in
full rather than cursor-paginated.

GET /api/v2/audiences/{id}/members — the contacts in an audience.

``{id}`` is an audience id, or the reserved ``all`` for every active
subscriber in the workspace. Cursor-paginated (ordered by the indexed
Person id) so a client can iterate an audience of any size. One-time send
audiences (``ad_hoc``) are not addressable here, matching the audience list.

/api/v2/automations/{event,events} — custom automation trigger events.

- GET /api/v2/automations/events lists the workspace's custom event
  definitions (name + payload schema), so a client can discover which
  events it may fire.
- POST /api/v2/automations/event fires a custom trigger (v2 port of the
  legacy POST /api/automations/event/): 202 (processed async), 404/400 via
  the v2 envelope, Idempotency-Key support.

get.description:
GET /api/v2/health — public liveness / readiness probe.

Deliberately NOT a ``V2ViewMixin`` view: it's unauthenticated and
throttle-exempt so external uptime monitors can hit it without an API key
and without ever being rate-limited (a health check must always be able to
answer).

By default it's a pure *liveness* check — no dependency I/O — returning
``200 {"status": "ok"}`` as long as the process can serve requests. Pass
``?check=readiness`` (or ``?deep=1``) to also probe Postgres and Redis;
that returns ``503`` if either dependency is unreachable, with a per-check
breakdown. Failures are logged server-side; the response never echoes
exception details, so nothing internal leaks to an unauthenticated caller.

GET /api/v2/operations/{id} — poll an async operation.

Operation ids come from 202 responses (`V2ViewMixin.start_operation`),
which record the workspace that started them. Only that workspace can poll
an operation: any other id — another workspace's operation, an expired
one, or an internal Celery task id — is a 404. An id alone is not access.

/api/v2/people — resource-oriented contact management.

**A contact is addressed in the request body, not the URL.** Every
single-contact operation is a POST to /people or /people/<action> carrying
``id`` (the opaque uid) or ``email``:

==========================  ====================================
POST /people                create, or update an existing contact
POST /people/delete         delete
POST /people/opt-in         confirm double opt-in
POST /people/unsubscribe    withdraw email consent
POST /people/publications   read or update consent
==========================  ====================================

An email in a URL path is a liability. It lands in access logs, proxy
caches and browser history — an identifier that is also personal data has
no business being there. And characters that are legal in an address are
structural in a URL: ``/``, ``?``, ``#`` and ``%`` have to be
percent-encoded, and a path segment is the one part of a request no HTTP
client escapes for you, so getting it wrong reads as a missing contact
rather than a malformed request. A JSON body has neither problem, and lets
one endpoint accept either identifier by name instead of by heuristic.

Every one of these resolves through ``_person_from_body``, so the two
identifiers, the tenancy boundary and the 404 behave identically across
all of them.

The path forms (GET/PATCH/DELETE /people/{id}, POST /people/{id}/opt-in,
POST /people/{id}/unsubscribe, GET/PATCH /people/{id}/publications) still
work and are not deprecated — they are simply no longer the documented
default. The URL identifier there is the uid OR the email, so a caller
that only knows the email never has to look the uid up first. They remain
the natural fit when you hold a uid and want a cacheable, resource-shaped
URL.

Beyond addressing: unlike the legacy /api/people/, list and detail share
one representation, creating a contact whose email already exists merges
the new data into that contact (returning 200 instead of a 409), and lists
use cursor pagination served by the (workspace, id) index.

post.description:
POST /api/v2/people — create a contact, or update an existing one.

Addressed by body. An ``id`` must resolve to an existing contact (404
otherwise) and may carry a new ``email``; an ``email`` that already
exists merges into that contact (200), and one that doesn't creates it
(201). ``tags`` and ``publications`` are additive here as everywhere —
neither is ever removed by a write that doesn't mention it. Use
POST /people/publications to withdraw consent.

POST /api/v2/people/delete — delete one contact, addressed by body.
POST /api/v2/people/opt-in — confirm double opt-in, by body.

POST /api/v2/people/publications — one contact's consent, by body.

Omit ``publications`` to read. Supply ``{"<publication_id>": true|false}``
to apply only the ids it names — which is why a write here can't be
expressed as a PUT of the whole map, and why the required scope
escalates to ``publications:write`` only once a map is present.

POST /api/v2/people/unsubscribe — same, addressed by the body.

``{"email": "person@example.com"}`` or ``{"id": "aB3xY7..."}``. Same
semantics as the detail route above (global suppression, idempotent,
SMS untouched) — this exists so an integration holding only an email
can unsubscribe without URL-encoding it into a path, which is the
shape most unsubscribe hooks in a caller's own app are written
against.

post.description:
POST /api/v2/people/{id}/unsubscribe — withdraw email consent.

``{id}`` is the contact's uid or their email address. A caller that
would rather send the identifier in the body has POST
/api/v2/people/unsubscribe (``unsubscribe_contact``) — same behavior.

The global suppression: the contact stops receiving every email from
the workspace (broadcasts, automations, transactional), which is what
an unsubscribe link does. To withdraw consent for ONE consent stream
while leaving the rest intact, use
POST /api/v2/publications/{id}/unsubscribe or
PATCH /api/v2/people/{id}/publications instead — global suppression
outranks per-publication consent, so this endpoint is the bigger
hammer of the two.

Idempotent: a contact who is already unsubscribed keeps the ORIGINAL
timestamp and no second ``person.unsubscribed`` webhook fires. The
withdrawal time is a consent record — a repeated call must not rewrite
when they actually opted out.

SMS consent is deliberately untouched: the two channels are consented
to separately (see ``Person.sms_consent``), so an email unsubscribe is
not an SMS opt-out.

Resubscribing is not exposed here — consent has to come from the
contact, not from an API key. POST /api/v2/people with their email
clears the suppression when you have that consent on record.

post.description:
POST /api/v2/transactional — send one draft to one recipient.

A transactional send: render an existing draft (by ``draft`` id) and email it
to a single ``email`` address. By default a recipient who is not already a
contact in the workspace is automatically added as an active subscriber, so the
send always has a deliverable target; pass ``add_contact=false`` to send
without adding them to the list.

Request body:
  - ``draft`` (required): id OR slug of the draft to send. Must belong to the
    API key's workspace. A slug is the draft title, slugified (readable
    handle); the id is resolved first so it always wins on the rare chance a
    slug collides with another draft's id.
  - ``email`` (required): the recipient's email address.
  - ``subject`` (optional): overrides the draft's title as the email subject.
  - ``preheader`` (optional): preview text.
  - ``event_properties`` (optional): one-off values for this send, referenced
    in the email by ``{{event.name}}`` tokens (event properties), exactly like
    an automation trigger's event payload. Not stored on the contact.
  - ``fields`` (optional): custom-field updates ({field_name: value}) written
    to the recipient contact before sending. These populate the contact's
    custom fields, which power ``{{merge.data_name}}`` merge tags. When
    ``add_contact`` is false and the recipient is not already a contact, the
    fields still feed this send's merge tags but nothing is persisted.
  - ``add_contact`` (optional, default true): whether to add the recipient to
    the workspace's contact list. False sends without creating a contact (and
    leaves an existing contact's list membership untouched).

The send is processed asynchronously: the response is ``202`` with an
``operation_id``/``operation_url`` to poll, plus the created transactional
email ``id``. ``Idempotency-Key`` is honored so a retried request never
double-sends. Sending is cardless — no payment method required; only a
blocked or delinquent (failed-payment) workspace receives a ``403``.
